supplemental.case: U09-controls.json: real shorter/base builds and exploratory52week extension
supplemental.scope: Supplemental production API controls; primary literal fourteen-day return remains unchanged.
findings: Shorter build changes race to 10K on 2027-02-28, clears the 4-hour marathon goal, and delivers 11.3 km longest/32.7 km peak with three introductory easy calendar weeks. Protected changes and audit failures are empty.

Base build has only easy future running, clears the goal, and supplies 10 km longest/29.8 km peak, but still contains a 42.195 km race row on 2027-02-28 with conditional-start wording. Removing a time goal does not resolve this endurance gap.

Exploratory extension builds to 2028-02-27 and still peaks at only 17.7 km longest/42.2 km per week. It is expressly not an offered/successful full-preparation option and must not be reported as solving readiness.

The exploratory cap supports the product inability to offer an extension at this fixed base, not a conclusion that the runner could never improve readiness through separately confirmed base development.

remainingConcerns: The retained 2027-02-28 marathon row remains critically unsuitable if acted on as a race recommendation after an 8.8 km longest future exposure.
2026-12-06 full-cycle deadline falls within the return block ending 2026-12-13; it cannot imply a realistic full-marathon route at that date.
Extension unavailable under fixed generator/base rules does not mean the athlete can never train for a marathon after building a new base.
limitations: Literal log has sec fields in 18 entries out of 26; missing seconds remain unknown. Dates, kilometre and RPE evidence are not evidence of actual pace.
Synthetic domain-API replay on the supplied real-version packet, not observation of a real athlete, browser, database, cloud, watch or enforcement of a selected alternative.

old.assessment: The primary preserves records but has the coaching concerns listed below.
findings: Confirmed 28-day interruption since 2026-10-28 gives 33 km return base, future peak 47.4 km/week and longest 17.3 km.
Old descriptions retain strides on 2026-11-30, 2026-12-02, 2026-12-07 and 2026-12-14 although structured strides are absent.
The original substantial endurance programme cannot be treated as current post-break preparation; retained 2027-02-28 marathon needs a new readiness decision.

new.assessment: Reasonable explicitly limited return response; original marathon date and calendar remain a concern.
findings: B preserves 32 historical weeks while marking current returning readiness, and cleans all stale stride descriptions.
The dated four-calendar-week return period is 2026-11-26 through 2026-12-20, with conversational effort overriding the historical pace.

Final future preparation remains only 17.3 km longest and 47.4 km/week peak. B now expressly calls it limited and offers same-date HM without transferring marathon goal, or base; a full-preparation extension is unavailable under the current rules.

Retained full marathon race row is still present. A 2026-12-06 latest full-cycle deadline precedes completion of the stated four-week return block; the original date cannot be presented as a credible route from this block to full preparation.
